data.description:
## Problem

Best-effort tickets-branch push failures that are EXPECTED and AUTO-HANDLED are surfaced to
agent-visible stderr at WARNING with wording that primes LLM agent sessions to assume the store
is broken and burn tokens investigating. Two independent session reports on 2026-08-21 (multi-
agent burst, ~12 concurrent writers) show agents halting work to inspect `push.py`, hand-invoke
`commit_and_push_tickets_branch`, and reason about ref topology — for a state that heals on the
next successful write.

## Offending messages (all logger.warning, agent-visible)

1. `push.py:342` — "tickets branch push failed after 3 retries: <raw git stderr><suffix>" after
   losing a CONTENTION race. Raw git stderr passthrough includes phrases that pattern-match
   corruption to an LLM: `unable to update local ref`, `! [rejected]`.
2. `push_classify.py:225` — "tickets branch push hit a transient transport fault (attempt x/y),
   retrying" — the code is already retrying itself; WARNING is pure worry-bait (INFO material).
3. `push_state.py:148` `unpushed_summary` — the "(N unpushed commits on origin/tickets..HEAD)"
   suffix: (a) "HEAD" is the TRACKER's HEAD but a session reads it as its code worktree HEAD
   (one report literally burned a turn disambiguating exactly this); (b) the count escalates
   across ALL concurrent sessions, so each agent adopts the shared backlog as its own emergency;
   (c) nothing says "expected under concurrent writers; publishes on next write; no action needed".

## What must STAY loud (bug 2a76's rationale is still valid)

- Policy declines (hook declined, GH013, branch protection) — permanent, operator-actionable.
- Strict-mode callers — PushDeliveryError already raises; unchanged.
- A PERSISTENT/growing backlog — fsck PUSH_PENDING + the durable rebar-push-pending marker are
  the operator channels; a repeated terminal failure with a GROWING count may stay WARNING.

## Operator ruling (2026-08-21)

"If these issues are expected and handled automatically, we need to stop surfacing them to
sessions because it primes them to assume there's an issue and burn tokens investigating."

## Fix direction

- Demote expected/self-healing outcomes (contention loss with marker recorded; transient
  transport mid-retry) to INFO/DEBUG, and/or reword to state affirmatively: "expected under
  concurrent writers; committed locally; will publish on the next successful write; no action
  needed".
- Fix the `origin/tickets..HEAD` ambiguity: name the tickets branch, not bare HEAD.
- Keep WARNING for policy declines and for terminal failures with an escalating backlog.
- CONSTRAINT: two negative assertions (test_epoch_guard_matrix / test_epoch_guard_reconciliation)
  prove the literal "failed after N retries" line is ABSENT in their scenarios — the line is
  appended-to, never reworded (see push.py:331 comment). Honor or consciously retarget with the
  tests updated in the same change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A lost contention race on a best-effort write emits no WARNING-level message; the
      state remains observable via push_status()/fsck PUSH_PENDING/marker.
- [ ] Mid-retry transient transport messages are INFO or below.
- [ ] Any remaining backlog message names the tickets branch explicitly (no bare `..HEAD`)
      and states the self-healing contract in the message text.
- [ ] Policy declines and strict failures remain WARNING/raise, byte-compatible where tests pin them.
- [ ] Tests pin: expected-case silence at WARNING, worry-free wording, and the preserved loud cases.
data.title: Expected tickets-push contention warnings prime agent sessions to investigate non-issues
